politeAccess: HTTPS only, no credentials; at most one request start per 1.1 s per host (serial per-host queue), bounded envelopes and counts; outFields limited to native-ID, object-ID and ID-part fields.

identity.choice: nparno is NC OneMap's statewide key (stcntyfips + "_" + parno; every value matches 37___\_%), no blanks statewide. Unique in Greensboro; in Carmel Commons (Mecklenburg) 10 keys repeat but always with byte-identical geometry (collapsed by the adapter). parno alone is county-scoped.

earlierRuns.note: run before idBatchSize was set; descriptor otherwise identical

hostNote: services.nconemap.gov FeatureServer/1 and services.gis.nc.gov MapServer/1 publish the same NC1Map_Parcels layer (identical schema and record count 5,938,900 on 2026-10-12).
coverageCaveats: Native-ID IN predicates on this service take seconds per request (32 IDs: 10.6 s; 10 IDs: up to 3.7 s; 5 IDs: up to 3.9 s on 2026-10-12, Greensboro), so ID reads use batches of 5, matching the existing Wake County entry on the same service.
Some counties publish exact duplicate rows with identical geometry for one nparno (observed in Mecklenburg County); they collapse to one parcel. Distinct geometries under one nparno fail.
Same NC1Map_Parcels service as us-nc-wake-raleigh-parcels (served there from services.gis.nc.gov with stcntyfips=37183 and key parno); Wake County parcels would exist under both namespaces.
Layer also publishes owner, mailing address, sale and value fields, which are not requested.
